stories.title: DeepSeek Harness Desktop for macOS and Windows
stories.reason: DeepSeek shipping an official cross-platform (macOS/Windows) desktop agentic-coding harness is a real ecosystem move from a top open-weight lab, not just a model update; 383 HN points means most of the audience has already seen it, but a headline doesn't get marked down for that.

stories.title: From the creator of Redis; run LLM locally with ds4
stories.reason: antirez (Redis creator) shipping ds4, a tool to run LLMs locally, is exactly the 'running code from a credible builder, about how models are served' pattern the taste profile weights highest; 159 points and still low saturation for a niche-but-respected release.

stories.title: One month coding with GLM 5.3 Flash
stories.reason: A real month-long usage report on GLM 5.3 Flash (open-weight model) for coding is the kind of concrete, lived-with evaluation the profile wants over a benchmark press release.

stories.title: Sites in ChatGPT
stories.reason: OpenAI adding 'Sites' to ChatGPT (156 HN points, active discussion) looks like a new platform surface rather than a minor feature bolt-on; could not fetch to confirm scope, scored as a plausible headline pending more detail from the article itself.

stories.title: tigerless-labs/agent-memory
stories.reason: 2,292-star local-first, markdown-based long-term memory runtime shared between Claude Code and Codex, no API key — running code, serving-side agent infra, and enough traction to matter even though agent-memory is a recurring theme this week.

stories.title: Open-sourcing AstaBrief, the fast report-generation model in Asta
stories.reason: Ai2 open-sourcing AstaBrief, a small report-generation model, is a genuine open-weight release from a credible lab — the profile says always surface these, saturation is low since it's fresh and specialized.

stories.title: Show HN: Janus – Go binary that runs GGUF models via Vulkan on AMD/Intel/Nvidia
stories.reason: Janus is a Go binary running GGUF models via Vulkan across AMD/Intel/Nvidia — running inference code with real cross-vendor reach, squarely in the 'how models are served' lane, 93 points so still fairly fresh.

stories.title: Harvard particle physicist Matthew Schwartz drops 36 papers authored with Claude
stories.reason: A named Harvard physicist publishing 36 Claude-co-authored papers is a concrete, attributable data point on LLMs doing real research work, not a rumor — exactly the kind of verifiable claim the profile rewards even at modest (48) points.
